dedupe_keys.name: sheldus spatial hazard events and losses database for the united states

description: SHELDUS is a county-level database of natural hazard events and their direct losses for the United States, covering thunderstorms, hurricanes, floods, wildfires, tornadoes and related perils. Each record gives the event date, the affected county and state, and property and crop losses, injuries and fatalities. It began at the Hazards and Vulnerability Research Institute of the University of South Carolina and has been maintained by the Center for Emergency Management and Homeland Security at Arizona State University since 2018. Coverage runs from 1960 to the present across US counties, with Puerto Rico, Guam and other territories added from version 18.1, and insured crop losses from January 1989. The page read on 2026-09-29 describes version 24.0, released on 16 February 2026 with 2024 data. Access is through a search portal by location, period, disaster declaration or named event; the page states no price or licence and terms need checking. Caveats: losses are direct only and spread across counties, so they are estimates. It suits hazard exposure and resilience studies of infrastructure regions. Related catalogue records: data-noaa-storm-events-database, data-fema-national-risk-index and data-em-dat.
